# stable-diffusion.cpp
Diffusion model(SD,Flux,Wan,...) inference in pure C/C++ ***Note that this project is under active development. \ API and command-line option may change frequently.*** ## 🔥Important News * **2026/11/11** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds **Day-0 support for MiniMax-H3-Image** * **2026/10/16** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds **Day-0 support for MOSS-Image-Base / MOSS-Image-SFT** * **2026/10/16** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds **Day-0 support for FLUX.3 Image Klein / Klein Base** * **2026/09/20** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds **Day-0 support for Qwen-Image-2.1** * **2026/08/20** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **LTX-2.5** * **2026/08/04** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds **Day-1 support for MiniMax-H3** * **2026/06/25** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Krea2** * **2026/06/04** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Ideogram4** * **2026/05/31** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **PiD** * **2026/05/27** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Lens** * **2026/05/17** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **LTX-2.3** * **2026/04/11** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now uses a brand-new embedded web UI. * **2026/01/18** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **FLUX.2-klein** * **2025/12/01** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Z-Image** * **2025/11/30** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **FLUX.2-dev** * **2025/10/13** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Qwen-Image-Edit / Qwen-Image-Edit 2509** * **2025/10/12** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Qwen-Image** * **2025/09/14** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Wan2.1 Vace** * **2025/09/06** 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports **Wan2.1 / Wan2.2** ## Features - Plain C/C++ implementation based on [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml), working in the same way as [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) - Super lightweight and without external dependencies - Built-in [Web UI](./examples/server/README.md) for image and video generation - Supported models - Image Models - [SD1.x, SD2.x, SD-Turbo](./docs/models/sd.md) - [SDXL, SDXL-Turbo](./docs/models/sd.md) - [Some SD1.x and SDXL distilled models](./docs/models/distilled_sd.md) - [SD3/SD3.5](./docs/models/sd3.md) - [FLUX.1-dev/FLUX.1-schnell](./docs/models/flux.md) - [FLUX.2-dev/FLUX.2-klein](./docs/models/flux2.md) - [FLUX.3 Image Klein / Klein Base](./docs/models/flux3.md) - [MOSS-Image-Base / MOSS-Image-SFT](./docs/models/moss_image.md) - [Fibo 2.0 Dev](./docs/models/fibo2.md) - [Lens](./docs/models/lens.md) - [Chroma](./docs/models/chroma.md) - [Chroma1-Radiance](./docs/models/chroma_radiance.md) - [Qwen Image](./docs/models/qwen_image.md) - [Qwen Image 2.1](./docs/models/qwen_image_2.1.md) - [PiD](./docs/models/pid.md) - [LongCat Image](./docs/models/longcat_image.md) - [Z-Image](./docs/models/z_image.md) - [Z-Image L2P](./docs/models/z_image_l2p.md) - [MiniT2I](./docs/models/minit2i.md) - [P-H3-Image](./docs/models/p_h3_image.md) - [MiniMax-H3-Image](./docs/models/minimax_h3_image.md) - [SenseNova U1.5](./docs/models/sensenova_u1.md) - [Ovis-Image](./docs/models/ovis_image.md) - [Anima](./docs/models/anima.md) - [ERNIE-Image](./docs/models/ernie_image.md) - [Boogu Image](./docs/models/boogu_image.md) - [Krea2](./docs/models/krea2.md) - [Mage-Flow](./docs/models/mage_flow.md) - [SeFi-Image](./docs/models/sefi_image.md) - [HiDream-O1-Image](./docs/models/hidream_o1_image.md) - [Ideogram4](./docs/models/ideogram4.md) - [LLaDA-Image](./docs/models/llada_image.md) - [Ming-Image Design](./docs/models/ming_image.md) - [PixArt](./docs/models/pixart.md) - [Iris-3B](./docs/models/iris.md) - [Image Edit Models](./docs/guides/edit.md) - [FLUX.1-Kontext-dev](./docs/models/kontext.md) - [Qwen Image Edit series](./docs/models/qwen_image_edit.md) - [LongCat Image Edit](./docs/models/longcat_image.md) - [Boogu Image Edit](./docs/models/boogu_image.md) - [Mage-Flow-Edit](./docs/models/mage_flow.md#image-editing) - [LLaDA-Image Edit](./docs/models/llada_image.md#image-editing) - [Fibo 2.0 Dev / Edit Turbo](./docs/models/fibo2.md#fibo-20-edit-turbo) - Video Models - [Wan2.1/Wan2.2](./docs/models/wan.md) - [MiniMax-H3](./docs/models/minimax_h3.md) - [LTX-2.3/LTX-2.5](./docs/models/ltx2.md) - [HunyuanVideo 1.5](./docs/models/hunyuan_video.md) - [LingBot-Video](./docs/models/lingbot_video.md) - Video Upscale Models - [RelayVSR](./docs/models/relay_vsr.md) - [SeedVR2](./docs/models/seedvr2.md) - [PhotoMaker](./docs/models/photo_maker.md) support. - [IP-Adapter](./docs/models/ip_adapter.md) support (SD 1.5 and SDXL, including Plus) - Control Net support with SD 1.5 - [ADetailer](./docs/models/adetailer.md) - LoRA support, same as [stable-diffusion-webui](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui/wiki/Features#lora) - Latent Consistency Models support (LCM/LCM-LoRA) - Faster and memory efficient latent decoding with [TAESD](./docs/models/taesd.md) - Upscale images generated with [ESRGAN](./docs/models/esrgan.md) - Supported backends - CPU (AVX, AVX2 and AVX512 support for x86 architectures) - CUDA - Vulkan - Metal - OpenCL - SYCL - Supported weight formats - Pytorch checkpoint (`.ckpt` or `.pth` or `.pt`) - Safetensors (`.safetensors`) - GGUF (`.gguf`) - Convert mode supports converting model weights to `.gguf` or `.safetensors` - Supported platforms - Linux - Mac OS - Windows - Android (via Termux, [Local Diffusion](https://github.com/rmatif/Local-Diffusion)) - Flash Attention for memory usage optimization - Negative prompt - [stable-diffusion-webui](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui) style tokenizer (not all the features, only token weighting for now) - VAE tiling processing for reduce memory usage - Support for a wide range of [sampling methods and schedulers](./docs/guides/sampling.md) - Cross-platform reproducibility - `--rng cuda`, default, consistent with the `stable-diffusion-webui GPU RNG` - `--rng cpu`, consistent with the `comfyui RNG` - Embedds generation parameters into png output as webui-compatible text string ## Quick Start ### Get the executables - Download and extract pre-built binaries from the [releases page](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp/releases) - Or build from source by following the [build guide](./docs/build.md) The executable examples below run from the build directory (`cd build` from the repository root). Windows examples use the Visual Studio Release path; adjust the executable path for other build configurations or extracted archives. Model files stay under the repository's `models/` directory. ### Download model weights Choose a model from the [model guides](./docs/models/README.md) and download its weights and required components. For a simple example, save Stable Diffusion 1.5 under `models/checkpoints/`: **Windows (PowerShell)** ```powershell New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force ..\models\checkpoints | Out-Null curl.exe -L -o ..\models\checkpoints\v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors https://huggingface.co/stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5/resolve/main/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors ``` **Linux/macOS** ```sh mkdir -p ../models/checkpoints curl -L -o ../models/checkpoints/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors https://huggingface.co/stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5/resolve/main/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors ``` ### Option 1: Web UI Start the server: **Windows (PowerShell)** ```powershell .\bin\Release\sd-server.exe --model-dir ..\models ``` **Linux/macOS** ```sh ./bin/sd-server --model-dir ../models ``` Open , choose **SD 1.x** in **Recipe**, select the checkpoint, and click **Load models**. Enter a prompt and click **Generate**. See the [Web UI guide](./examples/server/README.md#web-ui) for the full workflow. ### Option 2: CLI Generate an image with one command: **Windows (PowerShell)** ```powershell .\bin\Release\sd-cli.exe -m ..\models\checkpoints\v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors -p "a lovely cat" ``` **Linux/macOS** ```sh ./bin/sd-cli -m ../models/checkpoints/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors -p "a lovely cat" ``` Run `.\bin\Release\sd-cli.exe --help` on Windows or `./bin/sd-cli --help` on Linux/macOS for all command-line options. See the [CLI guide](./examples/cli/README.md) for additional usage notes. ## Performance If you want to improve performance or reduce VRAM/RAM usage, please refer to [performance guide](./docs/guides/performance.md). For runtime and parameter backend placement, see the [backend selection guide](./docs/guides/backend.md). ## Documentation Browse the [documentation index](./docs/README.md) or jump to a topic: - [Getting started: build, Docker, CLI, and server](./docs/README.md#get-started) - [Models and components](./docs/models/README.md) - [Generation and inputs](./docs/README.md#generation-and-inputs) - [Devices and performance](./docs/README.md#devices-and-performance) - [Weights and quantization](./docs/README.md#weights-and-quantization) - [Troubleshooting](./docs/troubleshooting.md) - [Development and contributing](./docs/README.md#development) ## Contributors Thank you to all the people who have already contributed to stable-diffusion.cpp!

stable-diffusion.cpp

Diffusion model(SD,Flux,Wan,...) inference in pure C/C++

Note that this project is under active development.
API and command-line option may change frequently.

🔥Important News

  • 2026/11/11 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds Day-0 support for MiniMax-H3-Image
  • 2026/10/16 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds Day-0 support for MOSS-Image-Base / MOSS-Image-SFT
  • 2026/10/16 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds Day-0 support for FLUX.3 Image Klein / Klein Base
  • 2026/09/20 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds Day-0 support for Qwen-Image-2.1
  • 2026/08/20 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports LTX-2.5
  • 2026/08/04 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp adds Day-1 support for MiniMax-H3
  • 2026/06/25 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Krea2
  • 2026/06/04 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Ideogram4
  • 2026/05/31 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports PiD
  • 2026/05/27 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Lens
  • 2026/05/17 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports LTX-2.3
  • 2026/04/11 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now uses a brand-new embedded web UI.
  • 2026/01/18 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports FLUX.2-klein
  • 2025/12/01 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Z-Image
  • 2025/11/30 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports FLUX.2-dev
  • 2025/10/13 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Qwen-Image-Edit / Qwen-Image-Edit 2509
  • 2025/10/12 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Qwen-Image
  • 2025/09/14 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Wan2.1 Vace
  • 2025/09/06 🚀 stable-diffusion.cpp now supports Wan2.1 / Wan2.2

Features

  • Plain C/C++ implementation based on ggml, working in the same way as llama.cpp
  • Super lightweight and without external dependencies
  • Built-in Web UI for image and video generation
  • Supported models
    • Image Models
      • SD1.x, SD2.x, SD-Turbo
      • SDXL, SDXL-Turbo
      • Some SD1.x and SDXL distilled models
      • SD3/SD3.5
      • FLUX.1-dev/FLUX.1-schnell
      • FLUX.2-dev/FLUX.2-klein
      • FLUX.3 Image Klein / Klein Base
      • MOSS-Image-Base / MOSS-Image-SFT
      • Fibo 2.0 Dev
      • Lens
      • Chroma
      • Chroma1-Radiance
      • Qwen Image
      • Qwen Image 2.1
      • PiD
      • LongCat Image
      • Z-Image
      • Z-Image L2P
      • MiniT2I
      • P-H3-Image
      • MiniMax-H3-Image
      • SenseNova U1.5
      • Ovis-Image
      • Anima
      • ERNIE-Image

      • Krea2
      • Mage-Flow
      • SeFi-Image
      • HiDream-O1-Image
      • Ideogram4
      • LLaDA-Image
      • Ming-Image Design
      • PixArt
      • Iris-3B
    • Image Edit Models
      • FLUX.1-Kontext-dev
      • Qwen Image Edit series
      • LongCat Image Edit
      • Boogu Image Edit
      • Mage-Flow-Edit
      • LLaDA-Image Edit
      • Fibo 2.0 Dev / Edit Turbo
    • Video Models
      • Wan2.1/Wan2.2
      • MiniMax-H3
      • LTX-2.3/LTX-2.5
      • HunyuanVideo 1.5
      • LingBot-Video
    • Video Upscale Models
      • RelayVSR
      • SeedVR2
    • PhotoMaker support.
    • IP-Adapter support (SD 1.5 and SDXL, including Plus)
    • Control Net support with SD 1.5
    • ADetailer
    • LoRA support, same as stable-diffusion-webui
    • Latent Consistency Models support (LCM/LCM-LoRA)
    • Faster and memory efficient latent decoding with TAESD
    • Upscale images generated with ESRGAN
  • Supported backends
    • CPU (AVX, AVX2 and AVX512 support for x86 architectures)
    • CUDA
    • Vulkan
    • Metal
    • OpenCL
    • SYCL
  • Supported weight formats
    • Pytorch checkpoint (.ckpt or .pth or .pt)
    • Safetensors (.safetensors)
    • GGUF (.gguf)
  • Convert mode supports converting model weights to .gguf or .safetensors
  • Supported platforms
    • Linux
    • Mac OS
    • Windows
    • Android (via Termux, Local Diffusion)
  • Flash Attention for memory usage optimization
  • Negative prompt
  • stable-diffusion-webui style tokenizer (not all the features, only token weighting for now)
  • VAE tiling processing for reduce memory usage
  • Support for a wide range of sampling methods and schedulers
  • Cross-platform reproducibility
    • --rng cuda, default, consistent with the stable-diffusion-webui GPU RNG
    • --rng cpu, consistent with the comfyui RNG
  • Embedds generation parameters into png output as webui-compatible text string

Quick Start

Get the executables

  • Download and extract pre-built binaries from the releases page
  • Or build from source by following the build guide

The executable examples below run from the build directory (cd build from the repository root). Windows examples use the Visual Studio Release path; adjust the executable path for other build configurations or extracted archives. Model files stay under the repository's models/ directory.

Download model weights

Choose a model from the model guides and download its weights and required components. For a simple example, save Stable Diffusion 1.5 under models/checkpoints/:

Windows (PowerShell)

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force ..\models\checkpoints | Out-Null
curl.exe -L -o ..\models\checkpoints\v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors https://huggingface.co/stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5/resolve/main/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors

Linux/macOS

mkdir -p ../models/checkpoints
curl -L -o ../models/checkpoints/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors https://huggingface.co/stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5/resolve/main/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors

Option 1: Web UI

Start the server:

Windows (PowerShell)

.\bin\Release\sd-server.exe --model-dir ..\models

Linux/macOS

./bin/sd-server --model-dir ../models

Open http://127.0.0.1:1234/, choose SD 1.x in Recipe, select the checkpoint, and click Load models. Enter a prompt and click Generate. See the Web UI guide for the full workflow.

Option 2: CLI

Generate an image with one command:

Windows (PowerShell)

.\bin\Release\sd-cli.exe -m ..\models\checkpoints\v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors -p "a lovely cat"

Linux/macOS

./bin/sd-cli -m ../models/checkpoints/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors -p "a lovely cat"

Run .\bin\Release\sd-cli.exe --help on Windows or ./bin/sd-cli --help on Linux/macOS for all command-line options. See the CLI guide for additional usage notes.

Performance

If you want to improve performance or reduce VRAM/RAM usage, please refer to performance guide. For runtime and parameter backend placement, see the backend selection guide.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A pure C/C++ implementation for running Stable Diffusion and other diffusion models locally without Python dependencies.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Stable-diffusion.cpp provides a lightweight, highly optimized inference engine for generating images from text prompts using diffusion models. By porting the complex PyTorch architectures into raw C/C++, it eliminates massive dependencies and enables execution across diverse hardware environments. It supports a wide array of state-of-the-art models including Flux, Qwen-Image, and various SDXL variants. The project focuses on maximizing performance while minimizing memory footprint, making local AI generation accessible on consumer hardware.
keyFeatures: Zero Python dependency: Runs inference completely standalone in C/C++, simplifying deployment and avoiding environment hell.
Broad model support: Continually updated to support the latest diffusion architectures like Flux, SD3, and Wan.
Hardware acceleration: Leverages CPU vector instructions and GPU backends like CUDA, Metal, and Vulkan for maximum throughput.
Low memory overhead: Implements aggressive memory management techniques to fit large models onto consumer GPUs.
Cross-platform compatibility: Compiles and runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux without complex configuration.

useCases.title: Local Image Generation
useCases.description: Run high-quality image synthesis on personal laptops or edge devices without needing a cloud API or heavy PyTorch install.

useCases.title: Application Integration
useCases.description: Embed state-of-the-art diffusion models directly into C++ applications, games, or native software products.

useCases.title: Resource Constrained Inference
useCases.description: Deploy generative AI on older or memory-constrained hardware where standard Python frameworks would fail.

useCases.title: Standalone Binaries
useCases.description: Distribute AI generation capabilities as simple, self-contained executable files.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: C++ developers, AI engineers, and enthusiasts wanting fast, local image generation. Requires basic command-line familiarity to run.
